cases.prompt: A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets

default.description: Best known SGLang command for the benchmark repo default profile.

h100-2gpu-ulysses-speed-eager.description: Hopper 2-GPU Ulysses/SP (sequence-parallel), resident, true eager — measured fastest for qwen no-CFG. torch.compile is a measured NET LOSS on this model.
h100-2gpu-ulysses-speed-eager.serve_args: --model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --dit-layerwise-offload false --tp-size 1 --ulysses-degree 2 --enable-cfg-parallel false --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile false
h100-2gpu-ulysses-speed-eager.policy_exception: compile OFF by measurement, twice over. (1) 2026-07-20 same-machine sweep (2xH100, 50 steps, ms/step): true eager 88.3 (4.54s e2e) vs 07-03-era compile 96.5 (4.97s) vs current-main compile 114.5 (5.83s) — qwen+compile never won (07-03 gain was ~1.5% at best) because inductor's triton GEMMs lose to cublas nvjet on this shape mix. (2) The 07-28 full-matrix run measured 5.74s under compile, matching the 114.5ms/step row: sglang PR #31849 (needed to stop a dynamo crash: can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope receives SymInt under tracing) additionally drops the fused qk-norm-rope kernel when compiling, so compile now also pays the unfused qknorm path x60 blocks. Until the fused kernel is made trace-safe upstream, eager is strictly faster AND numerically identical. Parallelism choice unchanged from 2026-07-03 ABAB x3: Ulysses 4.892 vs best-TP 5.135 (-4.7%, 3/3 pairs); TP-vs-Ulysses MAE 0.74/255 converging with steps = FP-reorder, not a bug.
h100-2gpu-ulysses-speed-eager.notes: Validated H100 only. --enable-cfg-parallel false required (no-CFG single branch; also prevents speed-mode auto-cfg from overriding sp_degree, PR #30016). speed mode auto-enables compile since #30016, so the eager exception MUST say --enable-torch-compile false explicitly. Campaign follow-ups (fused-qknorm dynamo fix, full-step CUDA graph, IPC A2A — notes/multimodal_gen/qwen_image_vllm_30pct_20260720.md) measured 3.952s on this case; revisit this profile once those PRs merge.

h200-2gpu-tp-speed-eager.description: Hopper 2-GPU TP SGLang qwen_image_2512_t2i_1024: resident DiT, compile-off (best-lossless). Same validated command as flux1/flux2 speed-compile.
h200-2gpu-tp-speed-eager.sglang_ref: origin/main + PR #29774 (QwenImage TP shard) + selective txt_mlp ReplicatedLinear (proposed #29774 follow-up)
h200-2gpu-tp-speed-eager.notes: no-CFG single-branch: TP shard (#29774) but keep text-branch txt_mlp ReplicatedLinear to skip its per-block all-reduce. Measured H100: full-shard 5.65s -> txt_mlp-replicated 5.076s, beats vLLM 5.17s. (true-CFG uses CFG-parallel instead — see the truecfg case.) offload-during-compile is in main. Selective-shard qwen_image.py kept at reports/h100x4-final-20260702/qwen_image_selective_shard.py. H100 superseded by Ulysses profile (measured faster). Ulysses was VALIDATED on H200 2026-08-26 and does NOT transfer: e2e ABAB x3 gave -1.0% / +5.9% / -1.0% (median TP 4.949s vs Ulysses 4.932s = 0.3%), mixed signs well inside the ~4-5% noise floor, so TP stays the H200 choice on measurement rather than by default. The remaining ~12% gap to vLLM-Omni (sglang 4.90s server vs 4.36s) is not a parallelism-strategy choice: txt_mlp replication is already active at tp=2.

h100-h200-2gpu-tp-speed-eager.sglang_ref: origin/main + PR #29774 (Shard QwenImage DiT across TP ranks; open, not yet merged)
h100-h200-2gpu-tp-speed-eager.notes: CFG parallelism is the cookbook-recommended Qwen multi-GPU path. Measured: 6.49s vs TP #29774 11.07s vs vLLM 10.14s (CFG-parallel 1.56x faster than vLLM). cases.label: MiniMax-H3 T2V+A
cases.prompt: At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.

default.description: Model-default topology; validate before publishing on hardware without a dedicated profile below.
default.notes: Mirrors the cookbook's 4x-class Ulysses4 resident recipe scaled to num_gpus; NOT validated at num_gpus=2 -- validate (incl. OOM risk) before publishing.
default.policy_exception: Correctness exception, not a speed tradeoff: MiniMax-H3's torch.compile path changes numerical output per the sglang cookbook (docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx, checked 2026-08-07) -- compile is not enabled by any recommended lossless preset for this model and must not be used to generate consistency ground truth. --enable-torch-compile stays false in every profile for this case until upstream fixes the numerics.

rtx5090-2gpu.description: 2x RTX 5090 (32 GB) layerwise-offload recipe -- the lightweight, broadly-runnable topology for this case.
rtx5090-2gpu.serve_args: --model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --model-variant fl2va --tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 1 --performance-mode memory --layerwise-offload-components dit,text_encoder,vae --dit-offload-prefetch-size 1 --dit-layerwise-resident-layers 20 --enable-torch-compile false
rtx5090-2gpu.notes: Matches docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx's verified 2xRTX5090/32GB/377GiB-host recipe as-is. The recorded numbers below (612.65s/556.79s/23366MB) were captured 2026-08-07 on minimax-h3-5090-2gpu-v4 from a run that used --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0 instead of 1, chosen at the time because prefetch-size 1 had intermittently deadlocked at 'Loading MiniMaxH3DiTModel ... Run:ai Model Streamer' on a minority of launches. That deadlock's real cause turned out to be unrelated to prefetch-size -- LayerwiseOffloadManager.__init__ clamps prefetch_size to min(max(1, prefetch_size), num_layers), so 0 and 1 are runtime-identical, and the 0-vs-1 correlation was coincidence (page-cache warmth carried over across attempts). The actual root cause: runai_model_streamer issues an unconditional torch.distributed collective (new_group + all_gather_object) inside find_local_ranks() on the first stream_files() call per component per rank, regardless of the is_distributed argument sglang passes (always False here); any per-rank divergence in layerwise-offload load order or timing can call that ad-hoc group out of lockstep and hang. Fixed at the sglang layer in sgl-project/sglang#33969 (monkeypatches find_local_ranks to skip the collective) -- serve_args here now uses the cookbook's prefetch-size 1 since 0 was never actually load-bearing; re-validate this cell once that PR lands to confirm the hang no longer reproduces even under adversarial per-rank timing. Client wall 612.65s, server-reported inference_time_s 556.79, peak_memory_mb 23366 (well under the 32 GB budget). --performance-mode speed excluded: H3's compile path changes numerics, and speed mode's residency assumption does not fit 32 GB without the layerwise knobs above. Single-GPU (num_gpus=1, tp_size=1) at this exact shape (1344x768, 124 frames) OOMs even at resident-layers=20 -- TP2's per-rank activation footprint (measured ~13 GB/rank at 100% util during a real denoise) roughly doubles unsharded on 1 GPU, on top of a 32 GB card already near its edge per the cookbook's own 2-GPU peak (~31.7 GiB/rank); the case is 2-GPU-only until that's independently reworked.
rtx5090-2gpu.policy_exception: Same correctness exception as the default profile (checked 2026-08-07): MiniMax-H3's torch.compile path changes numerical output per the sglang cookbook, so it is excluded regardless of hardware.

b200-2gpu.description: 2x B200 (183 GB), fully resident -- no layerwise offload needed at this memory class.
b200-2gpu.notes: Validated 2026-08-07 on 2 independent fresh 2xB200 devboxes (h3-b200-2gpu-v2 and its predecessor), same request as the rtx5090-2gpu profile. Two back-to-back runs agreed to 2 decimal places: client wall 80.64s/80.63s, server-reported inference_time_s 75.42/75.42, peak_memory_mb 108328/108358 (well under the 183 GB budget -- room to spare, unlike the 32 GB RTX5090 profile which needs the layerwise-offload knobs). ~7.6x faster wall-clock than the rtx5090-2gpu profile on the identical request; expected given B200's raw compute plus the total absence of the 5090 recipe's CPU<->GPU layerwise-transfer tax. See the vllm-omni entry's b200-2gpu profile for the cross-framework comparison on the same hardware.
b200-2gpu.policy_exception: Same correctness exception as the default profile (checked 2026-08-07): MiniMax-H3's torch.compile path changes numerical output per the sglang cookbook, so it is excluded regardless of hardware.

default.description: vLLM-Omni's own 2-GPU MiniMax-H3 recipe (TP2, distributed layerwise offload, compile path). Reaches health and accepts a request, then crashes during generation -- kept for provenance, not a working profile on any GPU class tested so far.
default.framework_ref: vllm-omni recipes/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3.md (2-GPU section); installed from git main (0.26.1.dev45+g24ede9e22 on RTX 5090, 0.26.1.dev50+gcfa6d66ed on B200) + vllm==0.26.0, not the repo's default pinned vllm-omni==0.18.0
default.notes: Requires ffmpeg/ffprobe on PATH for MP4 muxing. The request also needs `aspect_ratio` inside extra_params (the recipe's own T2VA example omits it and 422s with 'RuntimeError: t2va requires an explicit aspect_ratio' as written). CONFIRMED HARDWARE-INDEPENDENT 2026-08-07: re-ran this exact profile on 2xB200 (sm100, datacenter Blackwell) -- it segfaults with the identical signature as on RTX 5090 (native segfault, Python trace through torch Dynamo's custom_eval_frame), 1 step into denoising. Same bug on two unrelated GPU architectures rules out a consumer-GPU/SM120 quirk; this is a real vLLM-Omni MiniMax-H3 stability bug in the compiled path, not something fixable from the benchmark harness. Use the enforce-eager / b200-2gpu profile instead.

enforce-eager.description: Same recipe with --enforce-eager, tried after the default profile segfaulted. Fails differently (and earlier) on RTX 5090, but is the profile that actually works on B200 -- see command_profiles.b200-2gpu.
enforce-eager.notes: On RTX 5090 this crashes during server startup (EOFError: a diffusion worker process dies before completing its init handshake) rather than during generation, and never reaches a request. UPDATE 2026-08-07: the identical flags reach health and complete a real generation on 2xB200 -- see command_profiles.b200-2gpu for the hardware-scoped, validated version of this same command.

b200-2gpu.description: 2x B200, same recipe as enforce-eager -- the profile that actually completes a generation for this case.
b200-2gpu.framework_ref: vllm-omni recipes/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3.md (2-GPU section) + --enforce-eager; git main 0.26.1.dev50+gcfa6d66ed + vllm==0.26.0
b200-2gpu.notes: Validated 2026-08-07 on 2xB200 (h3-b200-2gpu-v2): completes the case's T2VA request end to end -- client wall 105.76s, server-reported inference_time_s 103.06, peak_memory_mb 24546. Output verified with ffprobe directly on the returned MP4: 124 frames @ 24 fps = 5.166667s, exactly matching the requested 5s/124-frame shape (the API's own JSON `seconds` field reported a stale '4' on both the submit and completed response -- a cosmetic metadata default unrelated to the real generation params, not a real duration shortfall; confirmed by decoding the actual file). Still uses the recipe's memory-constrained --dlo-resident-layers 20 offload even though B200's 183 GB has no need for it -- vllm-omni ships only one documented 2-GPU H3 recipe, so this is that recipe as-is, not a B200-tuned command; a fully-resident vllm-omni command may be faster but is not a documented starting point. Same request, same 2xB200 hardware, sglang's b200-2gpu profile: 80.64s/80.63s client wall, 75.42s inference_time_s -- sglang is ~1.31x faster than vLLM-Omni here.

vllm-omni.reason: Empirically validated 2026-08-07, first on minimax-h3-5090-2gpu-v4 (2x RTX 5090) then on 2xB200: the default (compiled) profile segfaults identically on both GPU classes 1 step into denoising (see command_profiles.default.notes) -- a confirmed hardware-independent vLLM-Omni bug, despite the recipe's own claim that torch.compile is 'not enabled by default on consumer paths.' --enforce-eager avoids that segfault, but on RTX 5090 it fails differently at startup (a diffusion worker process dies before completing its init handshake, surfaced as EOFError) and never completes a request on that GPU class. On 2xB200 the identical --enforce-eager command works cleanly and completes a correct generation -- see command_profiles.b200-2gpu for the validated numbers and the sglang comparison on the same hardware. Net: vLLM-Omni H3 support is real but fragile below the B200 class tested here; RTX 5090 has no working profile for this case in either variant.

report_framework_reasons.lightx2v: No MiniMax-H3 pipeline in LightX2V as of 2026-08; a turbo LoRA effort for H3 was blocked by the model license's territory clause (excludes EU/UK/South Korea/US), not by missing engineering support.
report_framework_reasons.trtllm-visual: trtllm-visual's tracked scope in this harness is image cases; H3 is a video+audio model.
report_framework_reasons.diffusers: MiniMax-H3 is integrated as Modular Diffusers blocks only (no DiffusionPipeline), and only via an unmerged PR (huggingface/diffusers#14355 -- pip install git+.../diffusers.git@refs/pull/14355/head). Not a servable baseline path today.
